names: North Fork Sauk Trailhead (FR-49, Sloan Creek Road)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass
Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency Pass for parking; Glacier Peak Wilderness regulations apply
drive: From Darrington, drive south on the Mountain Loop Highway about 16 miles, then turn east onto FR-49 and follow it 6.4 miles to the North Fork Sauk parking area.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required — $5/day or $30/annual.
Northwest Forest Pass required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
drive: From Marblemount, drive SR-20 east about 50 miles to Rainy Pass, turn left across the highway from the Maple Pass lot and go less than half a mile to the unpaved Pacific Crest Trail parking lot.

names: Tye Road pullout (old Stevens Pass Highway, Wellington)
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Skykomish Ranger District)
storedPass: Half Moon Crag: no fee site identified.
drive: From US-2 near Stevens Pass, drop onto Tye Road (old Stevens Pass Highway) toward the Iron Horse/Wellington townsite; park at the pullout below the crag

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Skykomish Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass required at developed trailheads.
Mount Index (Lake Serene/Bridal Veil Falls trailhead): Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass required. Half Moon Crag: no fee site identified.
drive: From Gold Bar, drive US-2 east about 7 miles and, where the road curves left toward the large bridge over the Skykomish River, turn right onto Mount Index Road. After a quarter mile on dirt, turn right at the sign for the Lake Serene trail; the parking lot is about 500 feet ahead.

names: Pinnacle Saddle Trailhead (Reflection Lakes, Stevens Canyon Road)
landManager: National Park Service — Mount Rainier National Park
storedPass: Standard Mount Rainier NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7 days), $55 Mount Rainier annual pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
NPS entrance pass / America the Beautiful pass
drive: From the Nisqually entrance of Mount Rainier National Park, drive Paradise Road about 15 miles to the Stevens Canyon Road junction, turn right and go 1.5 miles to the Reflection Lakes parking area.

landManager: National Park Service - Mount Rainier National Park
storedPass: Not a Northwest Forest Pass (that's a USFS pass and doesn't apply inside the park). Standard NPS entrance fee applies: $30/vehicle (7 consecutive days), $55 Mount Rainier annual pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
America the Beautiful pass or $30/vehicle entrance pass
drive: The road to Mowich Lake is closed to vehicles at the Fairfax Bridge on SR-165, which is closed to cars, bicycles and pedestrians; there is no alternate route and the park lists no other way in.

names: Hoh River Trailhead (Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center)
landManager: National Park Service — Olympic National Park (Olympic Wilderness)
storedPass: Olympic NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7-day), $55 annual Olympic NP pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
drive: From the Hoh River Trailhead (578 ft) up the Hoh River Trail

storedPass: Mount Rainier NP entrance pass (covered by park entrance fee / America the Beautiful pass) — Northwest Forest Pass does not apply inside the park

Not a Northwest Forest Pass (that's a USFS pass and doesn't apply inside the park). Standard NPS entrance fee applies: $30/vehicle (7 consecutive days), $55 Mount Rainier annual pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
drive: From Enumclaw, drive SR 410 east about 43 miles to the White River entrance of Mount Rainier National Park, turn right onto Sunrise Road and go about 5 miles, cross the White River, then turn left onto White River Road and follow it to its end at White River Campground.

From Bellingham take Highway 542 to Glacier, then go another 13.3 miles and turn left onto the unpaved Hannegan Pass Road just before the Nooksack River bridge near milepost 46. Drive about two minutes and park on the left. When the road is snowed over in winter, it is used for skiing and snowshoeing; park instead at the Shuksan Picnic Area at its base, where a recreation pass is required.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Cle Elum Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass ($30/yr) or America the Beautiful pass, or a $5/day pass at developed trailheads.
drive: From the Rachel Lake Trailhead (2,800 ft, end of FS Rd 4930 off Kachess Lake Rd, Exit 62 from I-90), start on Rachel Lake Trail #1313.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness, with some upper routes crossing into North Cascades National Park
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
drive: Start at the Twin Lakes trailhead (~5,200 ft), the rough, rutted end of Twin Lakes Road (many parties park short and walk the final rutted miles, as the road note indicates).

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District
National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)
storedPass: No day-use pass needed at Colonial Creek Campground/trailhead; the overnight backcountry permit is mandatory year-round for camping.
None
drive: Start at the Thunder Creek Trailhead at Colonial Creek Campground on SR 20 (turn in just past milepost 130).

landManager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)
storedPass: None — the Pyramid Lake trailhead is an NPS trailhead within the park complex, not National Forest land, so no Northwest Forest Pass/Interagency Pass is needed for day parking.
None for day use (no NP entrance fee); only the backcountry camping permit applies to overnight trips.
drive: From the Pyramid Lake Trailhead on SR-20 (6.4 miles past Newhalem; parking pullout on the left, ~6 cars, trail on the right side of the highway)
From I-90 take Exit 15 and drive south on 17th to a small pullout with room for about 5 cars.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
drive: From Winthrop, drive west on SR-20 about 27 miles (about 4 miles east of Washington Pass), turn right onto Forest Road 400, and follow it about 1 mile to the trailhead parking.
Driving north on Highway 155, pass the left turn into Steamboat Rock State Park and continue 1.3 miles to a big pullout on the right.

names: Slate Pass Trailhead (Harts Pass Road FR-5400)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at trailheads (e.g. Andrews Creek, Chewuch River) — $5/day or $30/annual.
None at the Monument Creek Trailhead. At the Slate Pass/Slate Peak and Harts Pass trailheads, carry a Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass to be safe.
drive: From the Slate Pass trailhead (~6,900', reached via the Harts Pass Road — one of the highest drivable roads in Washington), pick up the Buckskin Ridge Trail #498 heading north/northeast into the Pasayten Wilderness.

storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass ($30/yr) or America the Beautiful pass, or a $5/day pass at developed trailheads.
Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass typically required for trailhead parking.
drive: From Cle Elum, drive SR-903 north about 17 miles past Lake Cle Elum and turn left onto Road 4600 (Cooper Lake Road). Drive Road 4600 about 7 miles over Cooper Pass, then stay on Road 4600 about 3 more miles down to the trailhead.

Take I-90 Exit 47 and follow Denny Creek Road to the Franklin Falls trailhead when the road is open and free of snow. It is usually closed in winter; then a Sno-Park permit is needed for the pullout on the north side of eastbound I-90.

names: Necklace Valley Trailhead (East Fork Foss River)
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Skykomish Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass ($30/yr) or America the Beautiful pass, or a $5/day pass at developed trailheads.
drive: Park at the Necklace Valley Trailhead (~1,650 ft) at the end of FR 68 and start up Necklace Valley Trail #1062.

landManager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)
storedPass: No park entrance fee; parking at the Bridge Creek trailhead requires a Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass.
A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is required for parking at the Bridge Creek trailhead.
drive: From the Bridge Creek Trailhead on SR-20 near milepost 159, just over a mile east of Rainy Pass, south on the Pacific Crest Trail
